title: References and Symbolic References
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and boundaries of references and symbolic references.
Choose and interpret a Git command relevant to references and symbolic references using a disposable repository.
Verify the result with repository state or history and identify one safety limitation.

content.intro: This lesson introduces references and symbolic references as part of Git Internals and Object Storage. It follows the supplied Git curriculum and adds an original explanation, an inspectable command example, troubleshooting notes, and a practice task.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text:
**Core idea.** References and Symbolic References helps you apply a specific Git concept deliberately, understand its effect on repository state, and verify the outcome before continuing.

For **References and Symbolic References**, keep the named subtopics in view: Branch references; Tags; HEAD; Internal reference storage concepts. Treat those as the scope of this lesson, then practise the smallest workflow that demonstrates the idea.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: **Before you run a command:** decide what state you are inspecting or changing, identify whether the effect is local or remote, and write down what evidence would count as success. Inspect state rather than editing files inside .git by hand. Some commands differ depending on detached or unborn states.

content_blocks.title: Command example: References and Symbolic References
content_blocks.expected_output: The symbolic reference for HEAD when HEAD points to a branch; detached HEAD produces a different result.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Inspect state rather than editing files inside .git by hand. Some commands differ depending on detached or unborn states.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Use a disposable repository. If the exercise changes state, check git status and git log before and after; discard the practice directory only after confirming it contains no valuable work.
content_blocks.limitations: The CodeLeaf web lesson page does not execute arbitrary Git commands. Run commands locally in a disposable repository with a Git version appropriate to your task. Placeholder paths, branches, commit IDs and repository URLs must be replaced with values from that practice repository.

content_blocks.title: Safety and verification checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Start with git status --short --branch. For destructive or history-rewriting operations, review the exact target, create a recovery reference when appropriate, and keep valuable work backed up. Never put credentials, access tokens or private keys in course submissions.

task: In a disposable practice repository, follow the command example, capture the result, and write one sentence explaining how the result verifies the lesson’s concept. Keep unrelated changes out of the exercise.
hints: Use a read-only inspection command before any operation that changes files, refs or remote state.
After the example, verify with git status --short --branch and/or git log --oneline --graph as appropriate.
expected_output: The symbolic reference for HEAD when HEAD points to a branch; detached HEAD produces a different result.

common_mistakes.problem: Running a state-changing command without confirming the target repository or branch.
common_mistakes.why: A command may affect the wrong working tree or move a reference that other work depends on.
common_mistakes.fix: Check git rev-parse --show-toplevel and git status --short --branch before proceeding.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a command succeeded because no error was visible.
common_mistakes.why: Some Git commands are silent on success, and some expected actions are blocked by repository state or permissions.
common_mistakes.fix: Verify status, log, references, remote state or the named output explicitly.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an example placeholder literally or applying a destructive example to valuable work.
common_mistakes.why: Paths, branch names and object IDs depend on the current repository; restore/reset/clean operations can discard work.
common_mistakes.fix: Substitute real practice values, use a disposable repository, and preview changes before proceeding.

summary: References and Symbolic References is covered through these syllabus topics: Branch references; Tags; HEAD; Internal reference storage concepts.
Choose the command for the intended effect; understand whether it changes files, the index, local references, or remote state.
Verify the result, record unexpected output, and retain a recovery path for risky operations.
